provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03. Larry's son asked the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and reported this answer in his own words; third-person voice, so it is a paraphrase. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md.
text: Rank of interpreter is unknown. He doesn't know Vietnamese ranks. He seemed more of a buddhist than a soldier. Phonetically he says something like Trang-Zee-Nee-Yot-Na-Yong
researchNotes: Asked cold, with the reading held in research/people/trung-xi-nhat-nham.md deliberately not supplied. He did NOT separate a rank from the name, and says he does not know Vietnamese ranks - so this is not the independent confirmation the cold question was designed to produce. What it does give is a second, independent phonetic rendering: "Trang-Zee-Nee-Yot-Na-Yong" against the earlier "Trung Xi Nhat Nham". Both map onto the same sounds, and "Trang-Zee-Nee-Yot" fits Vietnamese "Trung si nhat", sergeant first class, closely. The reading is therefore better supported than before but still unconfirmed by him. "He seemed more of a buddhist than a soldier" is consistent with his earlier description of a warrior monk.
